speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you've presented with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. How long have you noticed these symptoms, and have you experienced any pain in your abdomen or chest?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, CEA, CA-125, CA-19-9, AFP

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 8,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL, Platelets 275,000 /μL; Comprehensive Metabolic Panel: NORMAL READINGS; CEA: NORMAL READINGS; CA-125: Normal; CA-19-9: NORMAL READINGS; AFP: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The diagnosis of pyelonephritis does not align with your large ovarian mass and significant abdominal girth; these findings are much more concerning for ovarian malignancy. While waiting for the tumor marker results, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as constipation or a feeling of fullness after eating small meals?

REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen and Pelvis with contrast
REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Scan_Results

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer with Malignant Ascites and Pleural Effusion

I note the tumor markers were normal, which is occasionally seen in early-stage disease or specific subtypes; however, the imaging showing a large mass and significant fluid accumulation confirms a serious pathology. Given the symptoms of shortness of breath and abdominal distension, would you agree to a therapeutic paracentesis to relieve the ascites and allow for fluid analysis?
